bio:
Obadiah Wells was born at Southold, NY, in November 1716, the second son of Henry Wells I, born in 1690, and a grandson of William Wells II and Elizabeth Tuthill. He left Southold at about 18 and took out a New York pedlar's licence on 23 June 1735. He married at East Hampton in August 1736, became a freeman of New York City in 1738, and worked there as a glazier and painter, also selling lottery tickets in 1749.

He later joined the purchase of a large tract of land at Brattleboro, where he was a proprietor and signed the Brattleboro declaration of 25 April 1777. He died at Montague, Massachusetts, on 27 May 1800, aged 83 years and 6 months, and was buried in the Old Burial Ground there, where his headstone stands beside that of his son, Dr. Henry Wells. He is John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed, both through William Wells and through John Tuthill.
sources: [R4-S1] Charles W. Hayes, William Wells of Southold and his Descendants (1878) (archive.org full text), ch. VI (secondary) https://archive.org/details/williamwellsofso00byuhaye

He is John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed through William Wells and again through John Tuthill (1635). He left Southold at about 18, peddled under a 1735 New York licence, became a glazier and painter (also selling lottery tickets in 1749), joined the purchase of a large tract at Brattleboro, and died at Montague aged 83 years 6 months.
summary: Southold-born pedlar who became a New York glazier and painter and a land proprietor at Brattleboro (1716–1800); John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed.
